title: Property Condition Disclosure Statement (PCDS)
description: Mississippi Code Ann. §§89-1-501 through 89-1-523 require the transferor of residential real property of not less than one nor more than four dwelling units to deliver a written Property Condition Disclosure Statement (PCDS) to the prospective transferee. The disclosure must be made on the form prescribed by the Mississippi Real Estate Commission (Miss. Code Ann. §89-1-509) and delivered as soon as practicable — before the buyer signs an offer to purchase or binding contract of sale. Disclosures must be made in good faith (Miss. Code Ann. §89-1-511). Certain transfers (foreclosure, fiduciary, between co-owners or spouses, court-ordered) are excluded under §89-1-501(2); MREC provides a Seller's Statement of Exclusion form for exempt transfers.

required_actions.note: Deliver MREC-prescribed PCDS before buyer signs the offer or binding contract. Exempt transfers under §89-1-501(2) should use the MREC Seller's Statement of Exclusion form.

title: PCDS Late Delivery and Amendment — Buyer Termination Right
description: Under Miss. Code Ann. §89-1-503, if the PCDS or any material amendment to it is delivered after the buyer executes an offer to purchase, the buyer has three (3) days after delivery in person, or five (5) days after delivery by deposit in the mail, to terminate the offer by delivering written notice of termination to the seller or the seller's agent. Sellers must amend the disclosure if conditions materially change before closing, which re-opens the termination window.

required_actions.note: Deliver any material amendment to the PCDS promptly; if PCDS or amendment is delivered after offer execution, honor buyer's 3-day (in person) / 5-day (by mail) written termination right.

title: Working With a Real Estate Broker (WWREB) Agency Disclosure
description: Mississippi Real Estate Commission Rule 4.3 (30 Miss. Admin. Code Pt. 1601, R. 4.3), adopted under the Real Estate Brokers License Law (Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-1 et seq.), requires licensees to disclose their agency relationship in writing at the first substantive meeting, using the MREC Agency Disclosure Form A ('Working With a Real Estate Broker'). Disclosed dual agency is permitted only with the informed written consent of all parties: the seller consents in the listing agreement's Consent to Dual Agency section, and both buyer and seller must sign the MREC Dual Agency Confirmation Form attached to the offer to purchase before signing/presentation of the offer.

required_actions.note: Deliver at first substantive meeting with any party the licensee does not represent.
Required only when operating as a disclosed dual agent; buyer signs before signing the offer, seller signs before the offer is presented.

title: Attorney Closing State
description: Mississippi is an attorney closing state. Miss. Code Ann. §73-3-55 makes it unlawful for any person who is not a licensed attorney to write or dictate deeds, contracts, or other instruments affecting title to real property for a fee or reward — so deed preparation, title examination/certification, and the conduct or supervision of the closing must be performed by a Mississippi-licensed attorney. Mississippi Bar Ethics Opinion No. 248 requires the closing attorney to clarify whom he or she represents and to act only as a scrivener if not rendering advice to a party. Title insurance is customarily issued on the basis of an attorney's title opinion.

required_actions.note: Engage a Mississippi-licensed attorney to examine title, prepare the deed and closing instruments, and conduct or supervise the closing.

title: Wet Funding Practice at Closing
description: Mississippi is a wet funding state by practice: loan proceeds are expected to be available and disbursed at the closing table, with documents signed and funds disbursed the same day. Mississippi has no standalone wet-settlement or good-funds statute governing disbursement; however, the Mississippi S.A.F.E. Mortgage Act (Miss. Code Ann. §81-18-1 et seq.) prohibits a licensed mortgage lender from failing to disburse loan funds in accordance with a written commitment or agreement to make a mortgage loan (Miss. Code Ann. §81-18-27). Closing attorneys customarily require collected/good funds before disbursing.

required_actions.note: Confirm lender funds are received as collected/good funds and disburse at closing per the written loan commitment; do not record or disburse prior to funding.

metadata.note: Wet funding is customary practice, not a statutory mandate; the S.A.F.E. Act citation governs lender disbursement conduct only.

title: Nonresident Seller Income Tax Withholding (5%)
description: Miss. Code Ann. §27-7-308 requires that, in a sale of real property (and associated tangible personal property) producing gross proceeds greater than $100,000 where the property is owned by a nonresident, the seller withhold from the sale proceeds and pay to the Mississippi Department of Revenue an amount equal to 5% of the amount realized on the sale (capped at the net proceeds otherwise payable to the seller). A corporation registered to do business in Mississippi is treated as a resident. The closing agent has no statutory duty or liability regarding compliance with this section, but should document the seller's residency status at closing. Excess withholding is refundable on the seller's Mississippi income tax return.

required_actions.note: If gross proceeds exceed $100,000, seller withholds 5% of the amount realized and remits to the MS Department of Revenue; document seller residency/registration status in the closing file.
Remit withheld amount to the Department of Revenue along with required federal information returns for the real estate transaction.

metadata.note: 2015 amendment (SB 2589) shifted the withholding duty from buyer to seller effective 2016 and gave closing agents a statutory liability safe harbor.

title: No State Real Estate Transfer Tax — Recording Fees Only
description: Mississippi imposes no state or local real estate transfer tax, deed tax, or documentary stamp tax on conveyances. The only government charges at recording are the chancery clerk's statutory recording fees under Miss. Code Ann. §25-7-9. Closing statements should not include transfer-tax line items for Mississippi property; verify FIRPTA applicability separately for foreign sellers under federal law.

required_actions.note: Record the deed with the chancery clerk of the county where the property lies and pay statutory recording fees; no transfer tax is due.
